attribution.note: The 200MW figure is Zitron's own reporting. He cites The Information for the one-year delay but adopts it as his own ('something I also said in October').

semantics.note: Combines a current-state observation (about 200MW) with a firm forecast that more power won't come for a year or more. Calling it a forecast is reasonable because the checkable part is the timing. Both parts are kept.

contract.note: The site-wide reading fits his context. He frames the expansion as everything past the first two of eight buildings, so 'that power' plausibly means power beyond about 200MW. The Information's narrower scope (six extra buildings) is flagged, and the result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: Oracle implied only about 200MW was operating as of April 22, 2026. This supports the current-state part.
In June 2026 Oracle said 42% of Abilene capacity (about 500MW) was delivered. This is a company disclosure.
The tracker cites Oracle's Sept 10, 2026 call: six of eight buildings delivered (618MW), 131k GPUs, and a model trained on site. This was well before March 2027.
Secondary summary saying The Information's one-year delay was about six expansion buildings, while the eight-building base build continued.

reviews.rationale: The about-200MW observation holds, according to Oracle's April statement. But the contract's early-resolution rule is met: Oracle reported about 500MW delivered in June and 618MW in September 2026, well before March 2027. That contradicts the forecast that more power wouldn't arrive for a year. 'Delivered' may not mean fully energized, but GPUs installed and training on site show substantial added power.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Broadly faithful, but it leaves out the 'entire market crystallised around a few companies' element and turns 'price tag' into 'built'. The contract's explicit elements put the missing element back.

contract.note: He named no measure. The contract's reading (OpenAI and Anthropic, majority share, inventory near $1tn, defined historical comparison) is ordinary but demanding, and it rightly refuses to invent a tolerance.

evidence.note: Company disclosure of a planned $500B Stargate investment. It is a plan, not built assets or an industry total.
Anthropic's $50B announcement with sites opening through 2026. It is a plan and doesn't establish a share.
MSCI found dot-com-era return concentration was higher on one measure. It doesn't test the combined infrastructure-and-tenant claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no nonduplicated infrastructure inventory near $1tn, no industry-wide denominator showing a majority serving OpenAI and Anthropic, and no matched historical comparison. The company announcements are plans, and MSCI covers market-return concentration only. The evidence available doesn't settle the claim.
